newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank/Portugal sees 1997 GDP growth 3.0-3.75 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank/Portugal sees 1997 GDP growth 3.0-3.75 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal said it expected economic growth of between 3.0 and 3.75 percent this year.
The central bank's quarterly economic report said gross domestic product (GDP) had increased 3.3 percent in 1996, above the government's forecast of a 2.8 percent rise.
It said Portugal would achieve price stability in 1998 and it did not foresee any significant inflationary pressures before the end of next year.
"Portuguese economic growth should maintain a rhythm in 1997 and 1998. For 1997 the Bank of Portugal forecasts growth of between 3.0 and 3.75 percent," the report said.

"Bearing in mind that there is usually some lag before the effects of increased economic growth have an impact on prices and salaries, significant inflationary pressures are not to be expected at least before the end of 1998," it said.
The central bank said prices would continue to come down next year.
